module.title: Managing the Technical Area
objectives: Know who may be in the technical area and how they must behave
Tell coaching from dissent and handle each correctly
Manage, then sanction — in the right order

blocks.transcript: Most of what happens in the technical area is normal — a coach instructing their team. Your job is not to police every word. It is to know the line between coaching and dissent, to manage the area calmly, and to sanction only when management has not worked. This tent talk is a five-minute refresher before you take the field.

body: A quick, tournament-side refresher on keeping the technical area under control — without making it a battle.

pages.title: What the Area Is
pages.subtitle: The bench, by the Laws — and the four rules that define it.

blocks.heading: By the Laws of the Game
body: The technical area — the bench or dugout — is the space outside the field for the named team officials, the substitutes and substituted players. The exceptions: when you allow a physio or team doctor on to treat a player, or when substitutes are warming up where you direct. At many levels it isn't even marked, and each team has its own. It exists for one reason — to reduce conflict with the match officials and the opposition.

blocks.title: What the Laws require
rows: At least 1 m (1 yd) from the touchline
No more than 1 m (1 yd) beyond the designated seating area on either side
Only one person per team may stand and give instructions at a time

pages.title: Who Belongs There
pages.subtitle: Only named team officials and substitutes — and one instruction at a time.

body: The technical area is for the named team officials and the substitutes, nobody else. Toggle each tab to see what each is allowed to do.

tabs.label: Head coach
tabs.body: May convey tactical instructions to their players.
bullets: One person conveys instructions at a time
Must behave in a responsible manner

tabs.label: Team officials
tabs.body: Assistants, medical staff, and other listed officials.
bullets: Only those on the team list may be present

tabs.label: Substitutes
tabs.body: Players waiting to enter or who have been replaced.
bullets: Subject to the same Law 12 offences as players
Warm up where the referee directs
Enter only with the referee's permission

pages.title: Coaching or Dissent
pages.subtitle: Instruction to your own players is fine. Aiming it at the officials is not.

blocks.heading: The one rule
body: Everyone in the technical area must behave in a responsible manner. Coaching their own team is allowed. Dissent, delaying the game, and leaving the area to confront an official are not.

cards.title: Responsible
cards.body: Loud, passionate instruction to their own players. Reacting to a decision without aiming it at you.

cards.title: Not responsible
cards.body: Dissent aimed at the crew, sarcastic protest, delaying a restart, or stepping out to confront an official.

pages.title: Manage, Don't Police
pages.subtitle: Small habits that keep the area calm long before anyone needs a card.

blocks.heading: Five habits that keep it calm
items: Manage early — a calm word at the first sign beats a sanction later.
One voice: hold them to one person standing and giving instructions at a time.
Keep them in the area — a coach drifting toward the field or the officials is your cue to step in.
Make it about behaviour, not the person: 'Coach, stay in your area and I'll keep the game moving.'
Lean on your crew — your assistant or fourth official can help hold the line.

blocks.heading: The order never changes
body: Manage first. Warn if it continues. Dismiss only when management has failed — and record it in your match report.

pages.title: When a Coach Reacts
pages.subtitle: A quick read in the moment — and what each read gets.

nodes.text: A coach reacts loudly to a decision.
Is it instruction to their own players, or is it aimed at the crew?
Own players: responsible behaviour. Let it go — keep refereeing.
Aimed at the crew: did a calm word settle it?
Settled: no sanction needed. Manage first, always.
Not settled: warn, then dismiss from the technical area for irresponsible behaviour.

pages.title: Know These
pages.subtitle: Three terms that decide how you handle the area.

blocks.title: Key terms
blocks.instruction: Tap each card to flip it.

cards.back: The area by the team bench — often unmarked — where listed officials and subs may be, and must stay.
The standard everyone in the area must meet. Breaching it is managed, then sanctioned.
Removing a team official from the technical area for irresponsible behaviour — recorded in the match report.

pages.title: Before You Go
pages.subtitle: Your checklist for the next match.

blocks.heading: The whole talk in three moves
items: Read whether a reaction is aimed at the crew.
Manage first; sanction (dismissal) only if management fails.

blocks.heading: Before you go — I will:
items: Let coaches coach their own players
Separate dissent from passion before reacting
Manage with a calm word before any sanction
Record any dismissal in my match report
